memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And he has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others. He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weavers - all of them skilled workers and designers.'" - Exod 35:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gave Bezalel and Oholiab extraordinary skill. Then He gave them something arguably greater: "the ability to teach others."

Talent that stays in one pair of hands dies with that person. Talent that is taught multiplies for generations. God deliberately built reproduction into the tabernacle project.

That is His pattern throughout Scripture. Moses trained Joshua. Elijah trained Elisha. Jesus poured Himself into twelve. Paul told Timothy to entrust what he had learned to reliable people who would themselves be qualified to teach others (2 Tim 2:2) — four generations in a single verse.

Notice also the pairing: Bezalel from Judah, Oholiab from Dan. Judah was the leading tribe; Dan was not. God joins them as partners in the same work. His teams are not built along the lines of status we would choose.

The question this raises is simple and searching. Who is learning from you? Not in a formal sense necessarily — who is watching how you handle money, disappointment, prayer, marriage, failure?

And who are you learning from? Both directions matter. A chapter that began with willing hearts ends with the reminder that God's work is meant to outlast the people doing it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who is currently learning something from you, whether you intended it or not?
2. What has God given you that you should be passing on?
3. Who could you deliberately invest in over the next year?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me pass on what You have given me. Let Your work in me outlast me. Amen.
